**Summary of what I did and why**

I read Apple's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2023-09-30) and checked the live quote, which showed AAPL at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) as of 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06. The filing showed FY2023 total net sales of $383,285M, operating income of $114,301M, net income of $96,995M, diluted EPS of $6.13, and net cash from operating activities of $110,543M. Net sales were down modestly from FY2022's $394,328M, but profitability remained very strong — a ~29.8% operating margin and ~$110.5B of operating cash flow — and EPS still edged up to $6.13 from $6.11, reflecting share count reduction. At $222.70, AAPL trades at roughly 36× FY2023 diluted EPS, which is a rich multiple, so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. I placed one buy limit order for 22 shares at $222.72 — the current ask, so it's tight to market — for about $4,900, which stayed under the $5,000 per-order cap and the $10,000 daily cap, used only existing cash (no transfers out), and stayed within the AAPL/INTC buy-only universe. The order filled at $222.72; I now hold 22 shares of AAPL alongside my 20 INTC shares, with roughly $45,100 in cash remaining today.
